summary: Ralph Lilley Turner worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1906–1910), and held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1913), Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and SOAS University of London, serving as Director (1922–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist educated at Warminster, Uppingham, and The Queen's College, Oxford, studying under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at Oxford (1849), the Indian Educational Service (~1853–1885), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as Principal (~1861–1878).
Ralph Waldo Emerson was a philosopher who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1817–1821) and later at Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).

Ram Chandra Kak was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall, later serving at the Archaeological Survey of India, the Sri Pratap Singh Museum, and the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

Ram Karan Sharma worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned degrees from Patna University and UC Berkeley under Murray B. Emeneau, and served as vice chancellor at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), the Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mir'at al-Akhbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India, under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as Head of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1989–1994).

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Patna University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he held chairs at Patna University (1958–1973) and the University of Delhi (1973–1978), and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.
Rama Misra Shastri worked in Indology and philosophy, serving as an assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1882 and 1914).

Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Banaras Hindu, Allahabad, Agra, and Rochester, and under traditional teachers Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, he held posts at Allahabad (1962–1966), Rochester (1971–1976), and Hawaiʻi (from 1976).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Elphinstone College, Mumbai, and Göttingen, learning under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Elphinstone and Deccan College, and served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist educated at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India, the University of Calcutta, and the Indian Museum (1921–1932), and presided over the Indian Anthropological Institute.

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur, vice chancellor at Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati (~1984–1987), and chancellor of National Sanskrit University (~2006–2010).
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at L.D. Arts College (attested 1938) and Gujarat Vidyapith.

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist educated at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He held positions at Fergusson College, served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001), and was a professor and dean at Pune University.

Ramendra Sundar Tribedi was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (~1882–1887) and served as Principal of Surendranath College (1892), also holding a post at Presidency University.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held faculty posts at Calcutta and Dhaka, where he was also Provost, and served as Principal at Banaras Hindu University and Nagpur University.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1967 he was attested as Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.

Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
